extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, corporate/agency/nonprofit/education communications teams and potential award entrants
extracted.subtask_description: Information about the PRWeek Awards 2026 — who is eligible, what the awards honor, and the kinds of work/people the program recognizes (e.g., most effective PR work, Communicator of the Year). Useful for teams preparing entries or assessing fit for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award focus: 'best of the best' and 'most effective work'
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRWeek Awards "will honor the best of the best corporate, agency, nonprofit and education teams, and the most effective work produced during the entry period."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries are evaluated with emphasis on being among the top-performing teams and on demonstrable effectiveness of the work within the stated entry period. The page states: "Winning entries can truly claim that they are the best of the best in the PR industry..." (promotional language implying a high bar for impact and outcomes). No explicit scoring rubric provided on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible entrants: corporate, agency, nonprofit and education teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility emphasis: the awards "honor the best of the best corporate, agency, nonprofit and education teams."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied requirement that submitting organizations/teams fall into one of these categories and that the work submitted was produced during the entry period. The page does not list additional formal eligibility rules or category definitions here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicator of the Year — demonstrated storytelling, reach and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Profile of 2026 Communicator of the Year Brandon Stanton highlights attributes: storyteller and photographer; creator of an online project with "thirty-million followers"; "inspired thousands of similar projects"; credited with "sparking a storytelling movement"; helped raise over $20 million; author of multiple #1 NYT Bestselling Books; creator of large public installations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Though not an explicit checklist, the bio implies criteria for this honor include exceptional storytelling ability, large audience reach, cultural influence/innovation, measurable social impact (fundraising/benefit to causes), and significant creative output. Use these attributes as indicators of the sort of impact/achievement considered for Communicator of the Year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury composition and peer review element
rubrics_metrics.description: The event names a Jury Chair (Kelly McGinnis, SVP & Chief Communications Officer | Levi Strauss & Co.) and notes that "Past winners are invited back as judges," indicating industry practitioners comprise the judging panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judging is conducted by senior communications professionals and past award winners, suggesting assessments will be practitioner-led and influenced by industry standards and experience. The page does not publish a detailed judging rubric or scoring weights; entrants should expect peer evaluation of strategic effectiveness and professional excellence.
